items.title: NHRC: Who will keep the keeper?
items.summary: On October 12, as the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) marked its 33rd Foundation Day. Its Chairperson, Justice V Ramasubramanian, described the office of the Chief Justice of India as one put to an agni pariksha (trial by fire) every minute, and “not necessarily by sacred souls”. Chief Justice Surya Kant offered a line that deserves to outlive the occasion: if the Constitution is the promise, the Commission is one of its keepers. It is a fine line. It also raises an uncomfortable question. Who ensures that the keeper is fit to keep? The question is not academic. Between November 9 and 20, the Sub-Committee on Accreditation of the Global Alliance of National Human Rights Institutions (GANHRI) will decide whether the NHRC keeps the ‘A’ status it has held since 1999. In 2025, the Sub-Committee recommended a downgrade to ‘B’. The Commission’s challenge was rejected in December. The concerns on record are familiar: an opaque appointment process, thin pluralism and gender representation, the government’s power to post a senior civil servant as Secretary-General and police officers investigating complaints against the police. items.title: Veeramani POCSO case: விசாரணை வளையத்தில் Arun IPS! | CM Vijay | Shabbir Ahmed | TNM Tamil
items.summary: The investigation into the POCSO cases against businessman R Veeramani has widened, and is raising serious questions now about how the Chennai police handled complaints against him. While the SIT continues to share details about private individuals arrested in the case, the Chennai police appear reluctant to disclose details of the inquiry involving its own officers. With no detailed public statement on the questioning of former Chennai Police Commissioner A Arun and former Additional Commissioner (South) N Kannan, questions remain over the transparency of the probe into the police department’s handling of the case. In this week's episode of Yen Endra Kelvi, Shabbir Ahmed examines the latest developments in the Veeramani POCSO case, the questions surrounding the police investigation, and the need for accountability when allegations of serious crimes involve those entitled to enforce the law.

items.title: Another rape, another suo motu cognizance, but what happens after?
items.summary: Recently, the Supreme Court, in a suo motu writ petition In Re: Recent rape incidents in Delhi NCR gave directions on institutional reforms for improving women’s safety in the Delhi-NCR region. The Court’s intervention comes in the aftermath of the alleged gang-rape of a 17-year old minor in Delhi’s Aastha Kunj Park. This is not the first instance the Court has taken suo motu cognizance of a matter concerning women’s safety against sexual violence. In 2024, the Court did the same in the RG Kar case and gave directions for the creation of safer working conditions for medical professionals. While such initiatives from the Court are admirable, a harder question to answer is: what happens after such directions are issued? The Court’s directions, without any corresponding enforcement mechanism, fail to achieve the aim that they are issued with. The suo motu cognizance addresses institutional failure as a common denominator in such instances of crimes against women. Pointing to the same, the Court also commented on how solidarity shown by the authorities is not the answer to this “ social evil ”. items.title: Second MRPL contract worker dies of burns suffered in September 30 fire
items.summary: Another contract employee of Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL) died on Saturday, October 17, from injuries suffered in the fire at the refinery on September 30. MRPL employees gathered outside the mortuary of a private hospital in Mangaluru, where the post-mortem was conducted. They identified the deceased as Rajesh D'Silva, 42. Rajesh was among 12 persons injured in the incident and had been undergoing treatment at a private hospital. He succumbed to burns on the morning of October 17. A resident of Kana in Idya village, Surathkal, Rajesh had worked at MRPL on a contractual basis for several years. He was unmarried. The fire broke out around noon on September 30 after a rupture in the cold separator, which operates at high pressure, in the Coker Hydrotreater Unit. The charred body of MRPL contract employee Manish Karkada, 30, was found after the fire was doused. MRPL had announced compensation of Rs 1.2 crore to Manish’s family. It also announced health insurance cover of Rs 5 lakh for each MRPL contract employee and his or her family members. items.summary: The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) has demanded the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and an inquiry into his conduct over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. At a meeting chaired by party president MK Stalin in Chennai on October 17, the party adopted four resolutions: Opposition to the SIR, support for protests against it, criticism of the Congress and the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), and a demand for electoral reforms. The DMK accused Gyanesh of overseeing the deletion of eligible voters’ names despite objections from the other two Election Commissioners. “He must be removed and subjected to an appropriate inquiry,” a resolution said. The party also demanded that the SIR be scrapped completely and that future elections be conducted using the electoral rolls prepared before the revision. It said the exercise should protect voters’ rights rather than deprive eligible citizens of their right to vote, and called for adequate time to be provided for adding and deleting names. items.title: UAPA no blanket bar on foreign travel: Delhi High Court allows riots accused Natasha Narwal to go to UK for PhD
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has allowed Delhi riots accused Natasha Narwal to travel to the United Kingdom for academic purposes and to meet her PhD supervisors. Justice Amit Bansal passed the order on October 16 and set aside the trial court order of October 6, which had denied her permission. While passing the order, the Court said that a case under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA) will not act as a blanket bar on a person's right to travel abroad. “The fact that the petitioner has been charged of serious offences under the UAPA does not curtail her right to travel abroad in a blanket manner,” the High Court observed in its order. Therefore, the Court allowed her to travel on a personal bond of ₹1 lakh with her brother as surety. Justice Bansal further said she will not seek asylum in the UK or comment on the cases against her. Justice Amit Bansal Narwal is pursuing PhD from University of Warwick and sought permission to attend an international academic conference in London, where her research paper, Gendered Carceral Labour as Social Reproduction, has been accepted for presentation. items.summary: The Angamali Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, on October 17, denied bail to the four accused in the Nedumbassery car accident that claimed three lives. First accused Suhail Sajeev (19) who drove the vehicle, and his three friends Ninav (19), Joel (20), and Ameer (20) will continue in judicial custody. Suhail had hit a two wheeler from the back while driving in the early hours of October 11 in Nedumbassery near Kochi. The crash resulted in the deaths of Gopika (22), Iyas (21) and Devika (21) who were part-time workers in an antique shop in Thrikkakara. The accident, a result of Suhail allegedly being drunk and driving rashly, has triggered huge public protests in Angamali. Suhail’s lawyer told the media that an appeal will be filed at a sessions court. While Suhail has been charged with culpable homicide not amounting to murder, his friends Ninav, Ameer and Joel are facing charges of abetment. The prosecution reportedly submitted evidence, including lab reports of blood and urine tests, showing alcohol use along with CCTV visuals of the accident.
